title: Potato Biological Genealogy — Hybrid Origin, Domestication, Introgression and Propagation
purpose: Represent potato ancestry as a reticulate graph rather than a simple tree: ancient hybrid origin, species radiation, domestication, wild-relative introgression, sexual recombination, clonal propagation and breeding all contribute to present potato genomes.
hard_boundary: Evolutionary history and biological inheritance are literal scientific topics. Project genealogical or theological interpretations are separate symbolic layers.

taxonomy.section_context: Petota contains tuber-bearing potato species and cultivated potato lineages.

deep_origin.finding: Genomic analysis published in 2025 supports an ancient homoploid hybrid origin of the Petota lineage from ancestors related to the Tomato and Etuberosum lineages about 8–9 million years ago.
deep_origin.evidence_scale: 128 genomes, including 88 haplotype-resolved genomes, in the cited Cell study.
deep_origin.biological_consequence: Complementary inherited parental genes contributed to the emergence of tuberization; sorting and recombination of hybrid-derived variation accompanied later species radiation.

domestication_and_diffusion.andean_context: Potato domestication is centered in the Andes and involved selection among diverse tuber-bearing Solanum germplasm over millennia.
domestication_and_diffusion.europe: Potatoes entered Europe in the sixteenth century; subsequent selection, bottlenecks and wild-relative introgression shaped European cultivars.
domestication_and_diffusion.phased_european_pangenome: A 2025 phased pan-genome built from ten historical tetraploid cultivars captured about 85% of haplotypes estimated to segregate in European potato and showed extremely high sequence divergence among haplotypes but a restricted haplotype space.
domestication_and_diffusion.wild_introgression: Modern cultivated genomes contain substantial wild-relative introgression, especially from breeding for disease resistance and adaptation.
domestication_and_diffusion.key_rule: A cultivar is not a pure endpoint of one linear ancestry. Its genome is a mosaic of inherited haplotype blocks with different evolutionary and breeding histories.

clonal.vehicle: seed tuber or viable tuber piece
clonal.effect: largely preserves an existing multi-haplotype genotype and linkage phase
gains: rapid fixation of elite heterozygous combinations

sexual.vehicle: flower → pollination → berry → true potato seed
sexual.effect: meiosis and fertilization reshuffle haplotypes and alleles
gains: purging or assembling alleles through breeding
costs: segregation breaks the uniform genotype of heterozygous tetraploid cultivars

breeding_genealogy.conventional_tetraploid: Crossing tetraploid parents creates highly segregating offspring because of heterozygosity, dosage, phase and tetrasomic inheritance.
breeding_genealogy.diploid_hybrid_direction: Modern programs also work at the diploid level to create inbred parents and F1 hybrids.
breeding_genealogy.self_incompatibility: Many diploid potatoes have S-RNase-dependent gametophytic self-incompatibility; the Sli locus and genome editing of incompatibility components are major routes toward self-compatible breeding material.
breeding_genealogy.design_rule: Every breeding claim should identify ploidy, parent material, propagation mode, and whether the result is a clonal cultivar, segregating population or true-seed hybrid.

query_examples: Which wild lineage contributed this resistance locus?
Which haplotype blocks are shared among European founder cultivars?
Is this relationship clonal continuity, sexual parentage or introgression?
Which genome regions descend from ancient Tomato-like versus Etuberosum-like ancestry?
